q: 1. If after every three or four stretchers, one header is used in a brick masonry wall, then the bond so formed will be called as
explain: English Garden Wall bond consists of several courses of stretchers followed by one course of headers (typically 3:1 or 5:1 ratio).

q: 2. The wall constructed along the slopes to protect the slopes of cutting from the adverse effect of atmosphere are called as
explain: Breast walls are designed specifically to prevent the weathering or 'slipping' of natural soil slopes, whereas retaining walls are meant to resist the active earth pressure of a backfill.

q: 3. The most important tool used by a mason in laying of bricks while constructing a wall is
explain: The trowel is the primary tool for lifting, spreading, and leveling mortar, as well as for 'tapping' bricks into their correct position.

q: 4. To protect the top of a parapet wall from the action of rain water, it is provided with a special course and that course if known as
explain: Coping is a waterproof covering (usually stone, brick, or concrete) placed on the top of an exposed wall to shed water.

q: 5. The material commonly used to cover the pitched roofs with steel trusses is ..........
options: thatched covering of reed or straw
explain: A.C. sheets (Asbestos Cement) or CGI sheets are the standard choice for covering industrial steel trusses due to their light weight and durability.

q: 6. The desired slope in Madras-terrace roofing is obtained by ..........
options: using varying thickness of brick bat concreting
using varying mortar thickness while laying flat tiles
adjusting the height of the furring piece at the centre
explain: In Madras-terrace roofs, timber furring pieces of varying heights are placed on the joists to create the necessary slope for drainage.

q: 7. The wedge shaped bricks or blocks used for the construction of an arch are called as
options: none of a, b and c
explain: Voussoirs are the tapered units that make up the curve of an arch; the center-most voussoir is specifically called the keystone.

q: 8. When rise of an arch is more than half of span of the arch and its lower portion is straight instead of circular, then it is called as
explain: A stilted arch has vertical 'stilts' below the curve, making the total height greater than half the span.

q: 9. When rise of an arch is more than the span, then the arch is called as
explain: Lancet arches are very tall and narrow pointed arches, where the rise significantly exceeds the span.

q: 10. In any case of the bearing of a lintel should not be less than
explain: The minimum structural bearing (overlap) for a lintel onto a wall is standardly 10 cm to ensure load distribution.

q: 11. A wall constructed to withstand the pressure of an earth filling is known as ..........
explain: Retaining walls are designed to resist the lateral pressure of soil or earth when there is a change in ground elevation.

q: 12. Arches over openings are preferred to lintel beams when
options: loads are heavy and span is large
explain: Arches are superior to lintels for wide spans and heavy loads because they act in compression, provided strong supports are present.

q: 13. Brick lintels are used when the span is
explain: Plain brick lintels have very low tensile strength and are restricted to spans of 1 meter or less.

q: 14. The angle of the skewback with the horizontal in the case of flat arches is usually
explain: For flat (camber) arches, the skewbacks are traditionally cut at a 60-degree angle.

q: 15. The lower half of the arch between the crown and the skewback is known as
explain: The haunch is the middle portion of the arch between the crown (top) and the springing (base).

q: 16. Normally the rise of the steps would be
explain: A riser height of 10cm to 15cm is standard for comfortable climbing, especially in public infrastructure.

q: 17. Air conditioning means ..........
options: cooling, purifying and controlling humidity of air
explain: Air conditioning involves complete 'treatment' of air, including temperature control, humidity control, and filtration.

q: 18. A facing and shelf, usually ornamental above the fire place is called ..........
explain: A mantelpiece is the decorative frame around a fireplace that often includes a shelf above it.

q: 19. For the construction of 10 cm thick brick wall, the bond preferred is ..........
explain: A 10 cm (half-brick) wall is built by laying bricks end-to-end, known as a stretcher bond.

q: 20. The exterior angle between outer faces of a wall, is known as
explain: A quoin is the external angle or corner of a building wall.

q: 21. A projecting piece usually provided to support a truss, is
explain: A cornice is a decorative and functional horizontal projection at the top of a wall.

q: 22. Expansion joints in masonry walls are provided if length exceeds ..........
explain: According to standard practice, expansion joints in long masonry walls are provided when the length exceeds 40 meters.

q: 23. The total horizontal force P per meter length of a retaining wall of height H holding a soil of density Y and angle of internal friction φ is given by ........
options: P = yH * (1 - sin φ)/(1 + sin φ)
P = yH * (1 + sin φ)/(1 - sin φ)
explain: Based on Rankine's Theory, the total pressure is (1/2) * γ * H² * Ka, where Ka = (1 - sin φ)/(1 + sin φ).

q: 24. The bricks used for face work shall be ..........
explain: First-class bricks are used for face work because they have uniform color, sharp edges, and a smooth texture, providing a better aesthetic finish.

q: 25. While calculating the loads, the specific weight of brick masonry is generally taken as ..........
explain: The unit weight of standard common brick masonry is approximately 1920 kg/m³ (roughly 19 kN/m³).

q: 26. The least thickness of a stone masonry wall is ..........
explain: Due to the irregular size of stones, the minimum practical thickness for a stone masonry wall is generally 350 mm.

q: 27. The wall constructed across the slope to protect the slope from the adverse effects is called ..........
explain: A breast wall is built to prevent the 'breasting' or sliding of natural earth slopes, whereas a retaining wall is designed to hold back artificial fills.

q: 28. The cavity wall is generally provided for ..........
explain: The air gap in a cavity wall acts as a barrier to moisture, heat transfer, and sound, significantly improving the building's internal environment.

q: 29. A temporary rigid structure having platforms raised up as the building increases in height, is called ..........
explain: Scaffolding is a temporary framework used to provide a safe working platform for laborers and materials during construction or repair.

q: 30. For a building on the side of a busy street where the ordinary scaffolding will obstruct the traffic on road, the type of scaffolding provided is ..........
explain: Needle scaffolding (cantilever scaffolding) is supported by 'needles' projecting from the wall, keeping the ground level clear for traffic.

q: 31. The brick laid with its length perpendicular to the face of the wall is called a ..........
explain: A header is a brick laid so that only its end (the smaller face) is visible on the surface of the wall.

q: 32. The brick laid with its length parallel to the face of the wall is called a ..........
explain: A stretcher is a brick laid so that its long face is parallel to the face of the wall.

q: 33. A system of providing temporary support to the party walls of two buildings when the intermediate building is to be pulled down and built, is called ..........
explain: Flying shores (horizontal shores) support two parallel walls across an open space without touching the ground.

q: 34. A brick which is cut in such a way that the width of its one end is half that of a full brick, is called ..........
explain: A king closer is formed by cutting a triangular corner of the brick such that the width of one end is half the width of the brick.

q: 35. A brick which is half as wide as a full brick, is called ..........
explain: A queen closer is obtained by cutting a brick lengthwise into two equal halves.

q: 36. Frog is defined as a ..........
options: depression on the top face of a brick
brick whose one end is cut splayed or mitred for the full width
brick used for the corner of a wall
explain: The frog is the indentation on the top face of a brick designed to hold mortar and create a mechanical key between courses.

q: 37. The most important purpose of a frog in a brick is to ..........
options: form keyed joint between brick and mortar
explain: By filling with mortar, the frog creates a strong 'key' that prevents the bricks from sliding relative to one another.

q: 38. In brick masonry, for good bonding ..........
options: all bricks need not be uniform in size
bats must be used in alternate courses only
vertical joints in alternate courses should fall in plumbs
cement mortar must have surkhi as additive
explain: Proper bonding requires that vertical joints are broken (staggered) so they do not form a continuous line of weakness through the wall.

q: 39. Cornice is defined as a ..........
options: horizontal course of masonry projecting from the face of the wall
horizontal moulded projection near the top of a building
covering placed on the exposed top of an external wall
triangular shaped portion of masonry at the end of a sloped roof
explain: A cornice is a decorative and functional horizontal projection that finishes the top of a wall or building.

q: 40. Coping is defined as a ..........
options: horizontal course of masonry projecting from the face of the wall
horizontal moulded projection near the top of a building
covering placed on the exposed top of an external wall
triangular shaped portion of masonry at the end of a sloped roof
explain: Coping is a protective cap (usually stone or concrete) placed on top of a wall to shed water and prevent moisture from entering the masonry.

q: 41. A bat is the portion of a ..........
options: brick cut in such a manner that its one long face remains uncut
explain: A brick bat is a piece of brick that has been cut across its width, usually classified as half-bat or three-quarter bat.

q: 42. Hearting is the portion of a ..........
options: brick cut in such a manner that its one long face remains uncut
explain: In thick walls, hearting is the interior portion of the wall between the exterior facing and the interior backing.

q: 43. A course of stone provided immediately below a cornice, is called ..........
explain: In classical architecture and stone masonry, the frieze is the course located directly underneath the projecting cornice.

q: 44. A course of stone masonry provided immediately above the cornice, is called ..........
explain: A blocking course is a heavy course of stone laid over the cornice to add weight and stabilize the structure.

q: 45. The type of stone masonry commonly adopted in the construction of residential building is ..........
explain: Coursed rubble masonry is popular for residential work because it is stronger and more aesthetically pleasing than uncoursed types.

q: 46. In the first class coursed rubble masonry ..........
options: all the courses are of the same height
minimum height of the course is limit to 150 mm
the length of the quoin is generally kept 450 mm
explain: First-class coursed rubble requires uniform course heights and specific stone dimensions for maximum structural integrity.

q: 47. The type of masonry in which the stones of irregular size and shapes are used and there are no regular courses, is known as ..........
explain: Uncoursed rubble masonry is the most basic form, where stones are used as they come from the quarry with minimal dressing.

q: 48. In stretching bond ..........
options: all the bricks are laid as headers
all the bricks are laid as stretchers
the arrangement of bricks is similar to English bond
the bonding bricks are laid at any angle other than zero or ninety degrees
explain: Stretching bond consists entirely of stretchers and is used primarily for half-brick thick partition walls.

q: 49. A type of bond in which all the bricks are laid as headers on the faces of walls, is known as ..........
explain: Heading bond uses only headers and is useful for constructing curved walls or footings.

q: 50. A bond consisting of heading and stretching courses so arranged that one heading course comes after several stretching courses, is called ..........
explain: Facing bond is used when expensive facing bricks are used for the outer skin and cheaper bricks for the backing.
